# Scope

Question: Which original studies compare player enjoyment (and related constructs) when competing against a believed-human versus a known-computer opponent in competitive games? Map designs, outcome measures, research foci.
T: 2026-01-27 (given explicitly; gateway bound = day before T)
Report language: en
Plugin: cs-ai (closest; none fits psychology/HCI games; openalex/crossref/europepmc/dblp cover it)

## Criteria
- Population: players in competitive games (video, board, sport-like, esports, Pong, prisoner's dilemma-like games only if competitive game framing, economic games excluded unless competitive game)
- Intervention/comparison: believed human opponent vs known computer/AI/bot opponent (includes deception/confederate designs, Wizard-of-Oz)
- Outcomes: self-reported enjoyment, emotion valence, motivation, flow, behavioral engagement, neural reward (fMRI/EEG)
- Types: English journal/proceedings original studies; dedupe identical experiments
- Exclusions: reviews after T; cooperative-only games; no human-vs-computer manipulation

## Angles
1. enjoyment/presence/social presence human vs computer opponent video game (HCI, CHI PLAY)
2. fMRI/EEG/neural reward, ventral striatum, competing human vs computer (neuroeconomics, rock-paper-scissors)
3. physiological/emotion/facial EMG, arousal, heart rate, playing against friend/stranger/computer
4. Agent vs avatar, believed-human vs AI (chess, Go, poker, Pong, Tetris, esports, exergames)
5. Motivation/flow/engagement, competitive exergames, cooperative vs competitive, bots in multiplayer
6. Variants: Turing test games, perceived opponent, mind perception, anthropomorphism, trust game/ultimatum (competitive)
7. Replications/negative results; earlier reviews

## Plan of findings (provisional)
1. Designs 2. Self-reported enjoyment results 3. Neural/physiological 4. Behavioral engagement/motivation 5. Moderators (agent realism, social presence) 6. Gaps
